nodes.name: CNTs ink preparation and coating
nodes.procedure: A mixture of CNTs, PVDF and acetylene black was prepared in a molar ratio of 8:1:1 and ultrasonicated for 30 min. The prepared mixture was evenly coated on nickel foam and dried in a vacuum drying oven at 60°C for 6 h.

unit_operations.name: Mixing and ultrasonication
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: A mixture of CNTs, PVDF and acetylene black was prepared in a molar ratio of 8:1:1 and ultrasonicated for 30 min.

unit_operations.name: Coating and vacuum drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The prepared mixture was evenly coated on nickel foam and dried in a vacuum drying oven at 60°C for 6 h.

nodes.source_text: A mixture of CNTs, PVDF and acetylene black was prepared in a molar ratio of 8:1:1 and ultrasonicated for 30 min. The prepared mixture was evenly coated on nickel foam and dried in a vacuum drying oven at 60°C for 6 h.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of NiSe@CNTs
nodes.procedure: Meanwhile, a 20 mmol L⁻¹ concentration of NiCl₂·6H₂O, 20 mmol L⁻¹ concentration of SeO₂ and a concentration of 5 mmol L⁻¹ LiCl were made into an electrodeposition solution. Finally, the nickel foam electrode with carbon nanotubes was placed in the electrodeposition solution and the NiSe@CNTs/NF electrode was obtained by electrodeposition at -0.8 V for 800 s with the help of the three-electrode method.

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition solution preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: a 20 mmol L⁻¹ concentration of NiCl₂·6H₂O, 20 mmol L⁻¹ concentration of SeO₂ and a concentration of 5 mmol L⁻¹ LiCl were made into an electrodeposition solution.

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the nickel foam electrode with carbon nanotubes was placed in the electrodeposition solution and the NiSe@CNTs/NF electrode was obtained by electrodeposition at -0.8 V for 800 s with the help of the three-electrode method.

nodes.source_text: Meanwhile, a 20 mmol L⁻¹ concentration of NiCl₂·6H₂O, 20 mmol L⁻¹ concentration of SeO₂ and a concentration of 5 mmol L⁻¹ LiCl were made into an electrodeposition solution. Finally, the nickel foam electrode with carbon nanotubes was placed in the electrodeposition solution and the NiSe@CNTs/NF electrode was obtained by electrodeposition at -0.8 V for 800 s with the help of the three-electrode method.

nodes.description: HER performance in N₂-saturated 1.0 M KOH (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic performance of NiSe@CNTs was investigated in an N₂-saturated 1.0 M KOH solution with the aid of a typical three-electrode system... iR-corrected HER LSV polarization curves... overpotential of NiSe@CNTs is only 27 mV... Tafel slope of NiSe@CNTs is only 46.2 mV dec⁻¹... 96.3% voltage retention after more than a month-long (upward of 730 h)

the optimal NiSe@CNTs catalyst exhibits incredibly high electrocatalytic activity toward OER, with overpotential as low as 145 mV to achieve a large current density of 100 mA cm⁻²... corresponding Tafel slope is the smallest value of 10.5 mV dec⁻¹... negligible degradation after more than one month of stable OER operation (97.2% retention rate over 730 h)

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1.0 M KOH (two-electrode, bifunctional)
nodes.source_text: the two-electrode system of NiSe@CNTs requires an ultra-low potential of 1.43 V to achieve a current density of 10 mA cm⁻¹... did not exhibit a significant voltage drop after 350 h of stable operation

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe@CNTs/NF shows characteristic NiSe peaks at 32.8°, 44.4°, 49.9°, 59.6°, 61.2°, 70.4° corresponding to (101), (102), (110), (103), (201), (004) planes plus CNT peaks at 26.3°, 42.2°, 44.3°, 50.4° for (002), (100), (101), (004) facets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of NiSe/NF and NiSe@CNTs/NF electrodes were shown in Fig. 1b. The NiSe sample exhibits the characteristic diffraction peaks at 20 of 32.8, 44.4, 49.9, 59.6, 61.2 and 70.4°, corresponding to the (101), (102), (110), (103), (201) and (004) crystal planes of typical NiSe (JCPDS 02-0892), respectively.

properties.description: X-ray diffraction pattern with multiple peaks labeled

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe content in NiSe@CNTs determined to be ~43.7 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S1, The NiSe content in NiSe@CNTs was determined to be ∼43.7 wt% by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) in the air.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe shows aggregation of nanoparticles masking active sites; NiSe@CNTs shows uniformly dispersed nanoparticles of 10-15 nm firmly fixed on CNTs network.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM image of NiSe shows that a large number of active sites are masked due to the close alignment and aggregation of nickel selenide nanoparticles... after introducing NiSe on the CNTs network, these nanoparticles are uniformly dispersed and firmly fixed on the CNTs.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe@CNTs shows nanoparticles entangled and separated by multiple carbon tubes with particle size 10-15 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 1f-g, the NiSe@CNTs heterogeneous structure can be further observed by the TEM test technique. The HRTEM image shows that the crystalline planes with a lattice spacing of 0.18 nm correspond to the (102) crystalline planes of NiSe.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of NiSe@CNTs shows lattice spacing of 0.18 nm corresponding to (102) planes of NiSe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image shows that the crystalline planes with a lattice spacing of 0.18 nm correspond to the (102) crystalline planes of NiSe.

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mapping confirms NiSe@CNTs composed of C, Ni, Se with NiSe nanoparticles wrapped by multiple carbon nanotubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1h, the element mapping results show that the NiSe@CNTs heterogeneous structure is composed of C, Ni and Se three elements, and the NiSe nanoparticles are wrapped by multiple carbon nanotubes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p spectra of NiSe@CNTs show Ni³⁺ and Ni²⁺ peaks shifted 0.5 eV lower binding energy than NiSe; Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ molar ratio 1.86 vs 1.12; Se 3d peaks negative shift indicating π-electron delocalization from CNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to the Ni 2p state in NiSe, the characteristic peaks of both the Ni²⁺ and Ni³⁺ species of NiSe@CNTs shift toward lower binding energies by 0.5 eV... The Se 3d_{3/2} and Se 3d_{5/2} two peaks of NiSe@CNTs also show a slight negative shift as compared to those of NiSe.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES of NiSe@CNTs shifts lower energy than NiSe indicating reduced Ni valence and increased electron density; Ni-Se bond length contracts from 2.11 Å to 2.06 Å in EXAFS; Se K-edge shifts toward Se foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3c, the Ni K-edge spectrum of NiSe@CNTs shifts to lower energy compared to NiSe, indicating a lower valence state of Ni... the main peak for NiSe@CNTs shifts to a smaller radial distance of 2.06 Å... Compared to NiSe, the spectra of NiSe@CNTs shifts slightly higher energy, which is closer to that of Se foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe@CNTs shows lower internal resistance and faster charge transfer than NiSe and CNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 5a, NiSe@CNTs catalyst exhibits lower internal resistance and faster fast charge transfer than single species (NiSe and CNTs).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe@CNTs Cdl-derived ECSA = 790 cm² significantly higher than NiSe (477.5 cm²) and CNTs (492.5 cm²), confirming increased exposed active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 5b, the NiSe@CNTs catalyst possesses the largest ECSA value of 790 cm², which is higher than that of NiSe (477.5 cm²) and CNTs (492.5 cm²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra collected to confirm presence of CNTs in NiSe@CNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra were collected with the aid of a microscope Raman system (Senterra, Bruker) with an excitation wavelength of 532 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pore size distribution and specific surface area characterized at 77 K.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface wettability of catalysts was observed by the SL 200KS model optical contact angle meter and their pore size distribution and specific surface area were characterized by a 3 H-2000PS1 specific surface as well as pore size analysis instrument at 77 K.

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface wettability/hydrophilicity of NiSe@CNTs catalyst observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface wettability of catalysts was observed by the SL 200KS model optical contact angle meter... the results of hydrophilicity and specific surface area test further corroborate the above characterization results (Fig. S3-S4).
